pull_request.title: Bring segment.rs back into alignment with original
pull_request.body:
This PR focuses on eliminating transcription issues in `segment.rs`. It also refactors the permission structure of `SegmentOwner` to carry borrowed slot owners/perms instead of values, preventing duplication. We can do a similar refactor in linked_list later. The remaining work on `io.rs` will be next.

Github has the whole stack of commits listed again here, I guess because there was still some `phaseII/verified` history involved, but after this we'll stick to main.

Pull request overview

This PR realigns and refactors several Verus-backed memory-management components, notably rewriting Segment/SegmentOwner ownership to avoid permission duplication, and updating VM I/O and page-table verification plumbing to match newer permission representations and invariants.

Changes:

  • Refactors frame segment ownership/permissions (SegmentOwner) to carry borrowed slot permissions (simple_pptr::PointsTo<MetaSlot>) and moves Segment specs into ostd/specs/mm/frame/segment.rs.
  • Reworks VM I/O typing and specs (VmIoOwner, VmReader, VmWriter, MemView interactions) including new fallibility markers and new deep-embedding spec module for VmSpace.
  • Adds/threads new page-table invariants around freshly allocated nodes (grandchildren-none, child-path rebasing) and updates related cursor/node proof code.

Reviewed changes

Seems that copilot suggests that we lack error handling 🤔

It somehow restore the original code of the Asterinas.
For example, the original code of VmReader<Fallible>::read_val is

    pub fn read_val<T: Pod>(&mut self) -> Result<T> {
        if self.remain() < core::mem::size_of::<T>() {
            return Err(Error::InvalidArgs);
        }

        let mut val = T::new_uninit();
        let mut writer = VmWriter::from(val.as_bytes_mut());
        self.read_fallible(&mut writer)
            .map_err(|(err, copied_len)| {
                // SAFETY: The `copied_len` is the number of bytes read so far.
                // So the `cursor` can be moved back to the original position.
                unsafe {
                    self.cursor = self.cursor.sub(copied_len);
                }
                err
            })?;
        Ok(val)
    }

Copilot makes a good point, the leaked permission would be an issue if we called the function from verified code. I was just working on that function already (there is a transcription error; the Ok(_) => Ok(buf) should be Ok(buf) => Ok(buf)) so I'll also make sure the permission gets rolled back.

review_comments.body: Yeah, this is just a WIP that I was playing with while waiting on a blocker from the `io` work, so take it with a grain of salt. I wanted to see how easy it would be to approximate a deep embedding in verus. A rigorous statement of soundness needs to do induction over arbitrary call sequences. Currently we make that argument on paper rather than in Verus, because Verus obviously can't quantify over functions. This file is an experiment in working around that limitation by defining each function identifier in a big enum and treating calls as transitions in a proof-mode state machine.

review_comments.body: `write_val` splits/advances `reader_owner` (via `reader_owner.split(len)`) before checking `self.avail()`. If the function returns `Err(InvalidArgs)`, the writer is unchanged but `reader_owner` has still been consumed/advanced, which is surprising and makes retries impossible. Do the `avail()` check before splitting, or restore/merge the owner on the error path so ownership only advances when bytes are actually written.

review_comments.body: `VmReader<Fallible>::read_val` consumes `writer_owner` via `split(len)` even if the read fails due to `InvalidArgs` (not enough remaining) or due to a page fault (cursor is rolled back, but the owner remains advanced). This makes the API hard to use correctly since permissions are lost even though no value was produced. Consider only splitting/advancing `writer_owner` after validating `remain()` and after a successful read, or add a way to recombine/undo the split on error.

@@ -0,0 +1,887 @@
+//! Deep embedding of the `VmSpace` API.
+//!
+//! `VmStore` is the abstract state of a caller of the [`crate::mm::vm_space`]
+//! API: it holds the [`MetaRegionOwners`] plus a registry of every owner
+//! object ([`VmSpaceOwner`], [`CursorOwner`], `VmIoOwner`) the caller
+//! currently has access to.
+//!
+//! [`Op`] is an ADT enumerating the public exec API of `vm_space.rs`.
+//! [`step`] is a single proof-mode dispatcher: `step(s, op)` requires
+//! `s.inv()` and ensures `s.inv()`. Because Verus chains pre/post
+//! automatically, induction over arbitrary call sequences is implicit: any
+//! program of the form `step(s, op0); step(s, op1); ...; step(s, opN);`
+//! typechecks iff `s.inv()` holds at every intermediate state.
+//!
+//! # Soundness boundary: `_embedded` axioms
+//!
+//! Each axiom named `<exec_function_path>_embedded` mirrors the `ensures`
+//! clause of one public exec function in [`crate::mm::vm_space`]. For the
+//! embedding to be sound, every `_embedded` axiom must accurately reflect
